scheme: kind: content|process|local-inquiry|mixed; fact_able 0-5 = how well 1-3 sentence illustrated facts can serve it; first pass + adversarial second pass (agreement 0.958), 2026-08-27; JHS G7-10 added 2026-08-28 (agreement 0.978, 4 challenger overrides)

G3-M-1.why: 'Science explains everyday things' is card-able with generic Filipino examples (rainbow, rice cooking), but the competency asks the learner to spot them in their own environment.

G3-M-2.why: Participating, questioning and tinkering is pure hands-on process; a card can only nudge the learner to go do it.

G3-M-3.why: Tool-use knowledge (a hand lens magnifies, a ruler measures length) is a clean one-illustration fact per tool.

G3-M-4.why: rag/sources/curriculum-guides/matatag-elementary-competencies.json:18 — verb is 'describe' process skills, i.e. declarative knowledge ABOUT a method, not performing it. One card can carry 'observing = using your senses, predicting = guessing what happens next, 1 m = 100 cm = 1000 mm'. Same class as G5-M-7/G6-M-9; the original treated 'describe' as if it were 'use'.

G3-M-5.why: Hard/shiny/stretchable properties of solids are textbook single-illustration facts.

G3-M-6.why: 'Burning plastic releases harmful smoke' is exactly a fact card.

G3-M-7.why: 'Demonstrate' is a doing verb, but the practices (recycle paper/plastic/glass, oil goes in the trash not the drain) are stateable tips.

G3-M-8.why: Shaping/hammering/cutting makes materials useful is illustratable (blacksmith, carpenter) though slightly abstract.

G3-M-9.why: Properties and uses of iron, gold, silver, copper are facts; the 'local community' angle is a light framing.

G3-L-1.why: Using observing/predicting/measuring in activities is a skill, not knowledge.

G3-L-2.why: Living vs non-living is a crisp fact; the observe-locally wrapper is minor.

G3-L-3.why: Living things grow, respond and reproduce is a one-sentence fact.

G3-L-4.why: Animal body parts and their roles (wings to fly, beak to eat) are ideal illustrated facts.

G3-L-5.why: Roots absorb water, stems carry it, leaves make food: classic fact card.

G3-L-6.why: Basic needs (air, food, water, shelter) is a plain fact.

G3-L-7.why: Interdependence examples (bees and flowers, carabao and farmer) are card-able; 'observe examples' is minor.

G3-L-8.why: Attitudinal, but 'protect habitats so animals survive' states cleanly as a fact.

G3-F-1.why: Explore-and-demonstrate is process, but 'wind moves a kite / a push moves a cart' are stateable facts.

G3-F-2.why: Exploring is process; the findings (rough surfaces slow objects, heavy objects are harder to push) are facts.

G3-F-3.why: Measuring and describing position change is a hands-on skill; relative-position vocabulary alone is thin.

G3-F-4.why: 'Sound is made by vibrations' is a perfect fact card; the explore verb is a wrapper.

G3-F-5.why: Sources of light and their uses are plain facts.

G3-F-6.why: Guided activity is process, but light behavior (reflection, shadows, straight-line travel) is fact-able.

G3-F-7.why: Harm from loud sound/bright light plus protection tips are clean safety facts.

G3-F-8.why: Guided activity is process, but examples (lighthouse, drum, hand signals) are fact-able.

G3-E-1.why: Locating things around school is local/process, but rocks, soil, water, air, clouds are generic facts.

G3-E-2.why: 'Glass is made from sand, bricks from clay' is a clean origin fact.

G3-E-3.why: Definition of 'earth materials' is a one-sentence fact.

G3-E-4.why: Observe-and-record over days is process and the patterns are local; only weather-type vocabulary is card-able.

G3-E-5.why: Weather effects on activities and dangerous weather are plain facts.

G3-E-6.why: Guided observation is process, but Sun/Moon/planets/stars are highly illustratable facts.

G3-E-7.why: Recording sky motion is process; 'the Sun rises in the east and sets in the west' is a fact.

G3-E-8.why: How Sun/Moon affect people (fishing by moonlight, farming by daylight) is card-able.

G4-M-1.why: A card about a Filipino scientist and invention is itself the secondary source the competency asks for.

G4-M-2.why: rag/sources/curriculum-guides/matatag-elementary-competencies.json:74 — source is restricted to 'the home or the local community' with NO secondary-source alternative (contrast G6-E-2 line 240 and G6-E-10 line 248 which say 'or other reliable sources'), and the target is 'their everyday life'. This is the clearest local-inquiry item in the set, more so than G6-E-3. A generic card (rice cooker / electric fan changed daily life) still supplies the content half, hence 3.

G4-M-3.why: Flammable, reactive, biodegradable are one-sentence property facts.

G4-M-4.why: Burning wood turns to ash and smoke is a clean fact.

G4-M-5.why: 'Demonstrate' is behavioral, but the practices (do not burn trash, handle bleach carefully) state as tips.

G4-M-6.why: Identifying own-community issues is local inquiry, but science solutions (composting, MRFs) are generic facts.

G4-M-7.why: Conducting a survey with classifying/communicating is pure process.

G4-L-1.why: Each body system in simple terms is a classic illustrated fact.

G4-L-2.why: Root vs shoot system and why they matter is a clean fact.

G4-L-3.why: Habitat classes with Philippine examples are facts; the diagram-making is a light wrapper.

G4-L-4.why: Listing is process, but 'mangroves shelter crabs and fish fry' is a strong fact.

G4-L-5.why: Flow-charting is process, but life-cycle stages are very illustratable facts.

G4-L-6.why: Herbivore/carnivore/omnivore grouping is a fact per animal.

G4-L-7.why: Drawing is process, but a Philippine food chain with labels is one illustration.

G4-F-1.why: Discover-and-predict is process; the content (soft things squash, rigid ones do not) is thin.

G4-F-2.why: Accurate measurement of distance and time is a skill.

G4-F-3.why: Definition of speed is a one-sentence fact.

G4-F-4.why: Constructing and labeling graphs is a skill; a card can only show what a flat line means.

G4-F-5.why: Guided demonstration is process, but pushes/pulls speed up, turn, slow or stop objects is a fact.

G4-F-6.why: Forces change shape (stretch, bend, twist, squeeze) is a stateable illustrated fact.

G4-F-7.why: Guided investigation is process, but magnet properties (attract iron, two poles) are facts.

G4-F-9.why: Energy causes change; light, sound, heat are forms: one-sentence fact.

G4-F-10.why: Observing locally is a wrapper; sources and uses of light/sound/heat are generic facts.

G4-E-1.why: Equipment-based comparison is process, but soil types and their water-holding are facts.

G4-E-2.why: Water is a basic need is a plain fact.

G4-E-3.why: rag/sources/curriculum-guides/matatag-elementary-competencies.json:117 — structurally identical to G4-E-1 (line 115, 'participate in guided activities ... compare soils') which the original labeled mixed/3; inconsistent to make this one process/2. The wrapped result ('loam grows plants best because it holds water and nutrients while draining well') is a one-illustration fact.

G4-E-4.why: Weather characteristics (temperature, humidity, wind) are definitional facts.

G4-E-5.why: Using instruments to measure and record is a skill; a card can only say what a rain gauge does.

G4-E-6.why: Chart interpretation is process and local, but extreme-weather safety precautions are facts.

G4-E-7.why: Sun composition, size and energy are textbook facts.

G4-E-8.why: Shadow-stick recording is process, but 'shadows are shortest at noon because the Sun is highest' is a fact.

G4-E-9.why: Discussion and source-checking is process, but importance of the Sun to life is a fact.

G5-M-1.why: Definition of matter is a one-sentence fact.

G5-M-2.why: Three states of matter is the canonical fact card.

G5-M-3.why: Shape/volume properties per state are plain facts.

G5-M-4.why: Classifying household objects by state is knowledge best served as a quick classify-this card.

G5-M-5.why: Using a measuring cylinder is a skill.

G5-M-6.why: Temperature drives melting/evaporation is a plain illustrated fact.

G5-M-7.why: rag/sources/curriculum-guides/matatag-elementary-competencies.json:136 — 'describe the steps' with the four steps enumerated in the text itself; the competency is recall of a 4-step list, which is exactly what a card can carry (did-you-know about a method). Doing an investigation is G5-M-9 (line 138), which correctly stays process.

G5-M-8.why: Using units is process, but unit facts (1 kg = 1000 g, water boils at 100 C) are card-able.

G5-M-9.why: Planning an investigation is a skill; only the anchor answer 'air has mass' is a fact.

G5-L-1.why: Digestive system parts and function is a classic labeled-illustration fact.

G5-L-2.why: Respiratory system parts and function is a classic illustrated fact.

G5-L-3.why: Factual, but a labeled reproductive diagram strains one engraving and the topic is AUP-sensitive for automated judging.

G5-L-4.why: Table-making is process, but group characteristics (mammals, reptiles, fungi) are facts best drilled as classification.

G5-L-5.why: Live birth vs egg-laying is a plain fact.

G5-L-6.why: Each life cycle is card-able; the three-way comparison needs more than one card.

G5-L-7.why: Purpose of tubers, thorns, bulbs, aerial roots is a fact per structure.

G5-L-8.why: Plant adaptations to drought/flood are plain illustrated facts.

G5-L-9.why: Mimicry and camouflage examples are ideal fact cards; the card is the secondary source.

G5-F-1.why: Carrying out investigations is process, but 'objects move in the direction of the push' is a fact.

G5-F-2.why: Plan-and-carry-out is the competency; 'rough surfaces make more friction' is only the wrapped result.

G5-F-3.why: Investigating is process, but friction makes heat and oil reduces friction are facts.

G5-F-4.why: Gravity as a non-contact force is a one-sentence fact.

G5-F-5.why: Heavy and light objects fall at the same rate (Galileo) is a myth-busting fact card.

G5-F-6.why: Effects of gravity on motion (things fall, thrown balls curve down) are facts; observe is a wrapper.

G5-F-7.why: Investigating is process, but 'a rubbed balloon sticks to a wall' is a fact.

G5-F-8.why: Assembling a circuit is a skill; a card can show the closed-loop idea but not teach building it.

G5-F-9.why: Designing a tester is process, but metals conduct and rubber/plastic insulate are facts.

G5-F-10.why: Making and recording an electromagnet is hands-on; only 'coil plus current makes a magnet' is a fact.

G5-E-1.why: Local identification is inquiry, but Philippine landforms and their influence are generic facts.

G5-E-2.why: Collecting and comparing rocks on school grounds is local hands-on process; only feature vocabulary is card-able.

G5-E-3.why: Classifying samples with a key is a skill; rock-type facts are only the wrapper.

G5-E-4.why: Soil forms from weathered rock is a plain fact.

G5-E-5.why: Demonstrate is process, but erosion moving soil by water and wind is a strong illustrated fact.

G5-E-6.why: Water cycle role is a classic fact card.

G5-E-7.why: Constructing a model is a skill; the water-cycle content is already covered by G5-E-6.

G5-E-8.why: Effects of typhoons and other disturbances are plain facts.

G5-E-9.why: Signal levels and their wind conditions are facts (use current PAGASA TCWS 1-5, not the older PSWS).

G5-E-10.why: Weather before/during/after a cyclone is a plain fact.

G5-E-11.why: Solar system structure and planet features are classic facts.

G5-E-12.why: Model-making is process, but moon phases with one Earth-Moon-Sun illustration is a strong fact.

G6-M-1.why: Melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation are plain facts; 'using diagrams' is presentation.

G6-M-2.why: Heat drives change of state is a one-sentence fact.

G6-M-3.why: Reversible physical vs irreversible chemical change is a plain fact.

G6-M-4.why: Solution vs suspension with everyday examples is a plain fact.

G6-M-5.why: Air composition is a one-sentence fact.

G6-M-6.why: Demonstrating is process, but each technique (winnowing rice, filtering, decanting) is a card-able method.

G6-M-7.why: Benefit of each separation technique (filtering makes clean water) is stateable per technique.

G6-M-8.why: Applying a fair test is a skill; a card can only describe it.

G6-M-9.why: rag/sources/curriculum-guides/matatag-elementary-competencies.json:202 — 'recognize the features of a fair test ... at least three trials' is declarative method knowledge; the doing counterpart is G6-M-8 (line 201, 'apply'), which is correctly process/1. A card 'Scientists change only ONE thing and repeat the test 3 times' carries this competency; keep at 3 because it is still method-flavored.

G6-L-1.why: Heart, blood, vessels and how they work is a classic illustrated fact.

G6-L-2.why: Pollination, seeds, propagation are plain facts.

G6-L-3.why: Planning a fair-test investigation on propagation is pure process.

G6-L-4.why: Vertebrate vs invertebrate with local examples is a plain fact.

G6-L-5.why: Roles in a food web are facts per role.

G6-L-6.why: Competition and predation examples are ideal fact cards; the card is the secondary source.

G6-L-7.why: Biotic vs abiotic factors is a one-sentence fact.

G6-L-8.why: Helpful/harmful interactions (pollination vs parasites, drought) are facts, though 'explain' spans several.

G6-F-1.why: Simple machines and their everyday uses are plain facts.

G6-F-2.why: Guided investigation is process, but 'a ramp makes lifting easier over a longer path' is a fact.

G6-F-3.why: Carrying out fair tests is the competency; lever facts are only the wrapped result.

G6-F-4.why: Waves carry energy from source to receiver is a one-sentence fact.

G6-F-5.why: Ripple-tank investigation is process, but crests, troughs and reflection are facts.

G6-F-6.why: Amplitude, frequency, wavelength are facts, but four abstract terms need one card each.

G6-F-7.why: Longitudinal vs transverse is factual and slinky-illustratable, though abstract for one image.

G6-F-8.why: Demonstrating with models is hands-on; the wave-energy content is already covered by G6-F-4.

G6-F-9.why: Sound is longitudinal, light is transverse: plain fact.

G6-F-10.why: Doppler effect with an ambulance siren is a great fact card.

G6-E-1.why: What volcanoes are and how they form is a classic illustrated fact.

G6-E-2.why: Nearest-volcano risk is local inquiry, but Philippine volcano locations (Mayon in Albay, Taal in Batangas) are facts.

G6-E-3.why: rag/sources/curriculum-guides/matatag-elementary-competencies.json:241 — the knowledge target is NATIONAL (eruption patterns in the Philippines over 100 years: Pinatubo 1991, Taal 2020, Mayon's frequent eruptions) and the predictability judgment is generic science; 'with family and community members' is the discussion medium, not the knowledge source. Contrast G4-M-2 where the home/community IS the source. Original's own card_form 'fact' concedes this.

G6-E-4.why: Lava, ash, pyroclastic materials are plain facts.

G6-E-5.why: PHIVOLCS alert levels and before/during/after steps are facts; 'demonstrate' is minor.

G6-E-6.why: Wet and dry seasons and fitting activities are plain facts.

G6-E-7.why: Globe demonstration is process, but rotation causes day and night is a strong fact.

G6-E-8.why: Model-making is process, but eclipses and seasons are each strong illustrated facts.

G6-E-9.why: Ancient use of constellations for direction and seasons is a plain fact.

G6-E-10.why: Primary path is indigenous community members, but the secondary-source option makes Philippine star lore (Balatik) card-able.

G7-M-1.why: 'Scientists use models for what cannot be seen' (globe, particle model) is a stateable nature-of-science fact, but slightly meta for a single illustration.

G7-M-2.why: The particle model statement is quoted verbatim in the competency and is a one-sentence illustrated fact.

G7-M-3.why: Particles move, have spaces, attract, and speed up with heat is a classic single-illustration fact.

G7-M-4.why: 'Use diagrams' is presentation (G6-M-1 precedent); solid/liquid/gas particle spacing is the canonical single illustration.

G7-M-5.why: Melting/boiling/condensing/freezing explained by particle arrangement and energy is one arrow-diagram fact.

G7-M-6.why: 'Follow' the steps is doing an investigation (contrast G5-M-7 'describe the steps'); only the enumerated five-step list is card-able.

G7-M-7.why: Making accurate measurements and organizing data is a hands-on skill (G4-F-2 precedent); a card can only name the SI units.

G7-M-8.why: Solute dissolves in solvent (sugar in water) is a one-sentence illustrated fact.

G7-M-9.why: 'Concentration = solute per volume' is a fact, but 'express quantitatively' is a calculation best drilled as a quick quiz.

G7-M-10.why: 'Demonstrate' is process, but 'sugar dissolves faster and more in hot water' is a stateable fact (G4-F-5 precedent).

G7-M-11.why: Text is 'identify solutions ... that react with litmus indicator, as acids, bases, and salts' — the verb is identify/classify and 'react with litmus' is a modifier on the noun 'solutions', not a doing-verb. Structurally the same as G5-M-4 'identify objects at home ... as solid, liquid or gas' (elementary: content 5 quiz). The original read the tool noun 'litmus' as a hands-on step. Contrast G10-M-2 where 'using different indicators' is an explicit adverbial method, which I leave as mixed 4. Card: vinegar/kalamansi = acid, baking soda/soap = base, table salt water = salt; classify-this quiz.

G7-M-12.why: Proper use and handling of lab equipment is a motor skill; only the safety and handling rules are stateable tips.

G7-L-1.why: Microscope parts and functions are a classic labeled illustration; handling and storing is a skill with stateable rules (two hands, cover it).

G7-L-2.why: Using microscope techniques to observe cells is a skill (G5-E-3 precedent); the cell-part content is the wrapper and is covered by G7-L-4.

G7-L-3.why: Bacteria are one cell, humans are many is a one-sentence illustrated fact.

G7-L-4.why: Plant vs animal cell by organelles (cell wall, chloroplast) is the classic side-by-side illustration.

G7-L-5.why: Mitosis for growth and repair, meiosis for sex cells is a plain illustrated fact.

G7-L-6.why: Half the genetic information from each parent via meiosis and fertilization is a one-illustration fact.

G7-L-7.why: Sexual vs asexual by number of parents and offspring similarity is a crisp comparison fact.

G7-L-8.why: 'Use a labelled diagram' is presentation; the cell-to-biosphere ladder is one classic illustration.

G7-L-9.why: Trophic levels as energy levels in a food pyramid is a one-illustration fact.

G7-L-10.why: Only about 10% of energy passes to the next level is a strong food-pyramid fact.

G7-F-1.why: Forces act between objects and are measured in newtons with a spring balance is a plain fact.

G7-F-2.why: Balanced vs unbalanced with the listed everyday examples (box on ramp, falling fruit) is a per-example illustrated fact.

G7-F-3.why: Drawing free-body diagrams is a representational skill; a card can show what one looks like but not teach drawing them.

G7-F-4.why: Unbalanced forces change speed or direction is a one-sentence fact.

G7-F-5.why: Distance vs displacement from a reference point (walking around the block) is a single-illustration fact.

G7-F-6.why: Speed vs velocity is a crisp fact, but 'using the concept of vectors' adds abstraction for one illustration.

G7-F-7.why: 'Uniform velocity = equal distance in equal time' is a fact, but representing it on distance-time graphs is a graphing skill.

G7-F-8.why: Heat is energy transferred, temperature is how hot, is a classic one-sentence fact.

G7-F-9.why: Helpful and harmful examples of conduction, convection, radiation are crisp per-mode facts.

G7-F-10.why: Particles bumping (conduction) and hot fluid rising (convection) is a one-illustration fact.

G7-F-11.why: The card is the secondary source (G6-L-6 precedent); heat-to-electricity devices (geothermal plants, thermoelectric generators) are facts, though 'innovative devices' is open-ended.

G7-E-1.why: Normal, reverse, strike-slip faults by angle and slip is the classic three-panel illustration.

G7-E-2.why: 'Use models' is process, but strain release causing earthquakes and the Philippine Fault being strike-slip are strong facts (G6-E-7 precedent).

G7-E-3.why: Bigger magnitude, bigger community damage (PHIVOLCS intensity scale) is a plain fact.

G7-E-4.why: Structurally identical to G6-E-2 (nearest hazard, local risk, 'or other reliable source'); the FaultFinder tool and the Valley Fault System are card-able, the learner's own nearest fault is not.

G7-E-5.why: Model-making is process, but focus vs epicenter, magnitude vs intensity, and undersea quakes making tsunamis are each strong illustrated facts (G6-E-8 precedent).

G7-E-6.why: 'Refer to the local disaster readiness plans to demonstrate what to do during and after an earthquake' — the original applied the G4-M-2 rule mechanically (source restricted to local, no alternative). But unlike G4-M-2, where the KNOWLEDGE TARGET itself is local (a home/community invention), here the knowledge target is universal: drop-cover-hold, move away from glass, expect aftershocks, check for injuries/gas, go to the evacuation area. The closer elementary parallel is G6-E-5 'Interpret PHIVOLCS alert levels to demonstrate what to do before/during/after an eruption' = content 4. 'Demonstrate' plus the local-plan source keeps it mixed rather than content, but a feed that carries a during/after-earthquake safety card serves this competency well, which local-inquiry would wrongly deprioritize.

G7-E-7.why: Undersea earthquake lifts water into a tsunami is a classic one-illustration fact.

G7-E-8.why: PHIVOLCS tsunami warnings, sirens, and run-to-high-ground procedures are national facts, though warning plus response spans two cards.

G7-E-9.why: Sunlight reflected, absorbed, and scattered by the atmosphere is one illustration, but 'explain how energy interacts' is broad.

G7-E-10.why: Physical model-making is process, but tilt causing uneven sunlight intensity over the year is a strong illustrated fact (G6-E-8 precedent).

G7-E-11.why: 'Using models' is process, but tilt changing daytime length across the year is a strong fact (G6-E-7 precedent).

G7-E-12.why: Land/sea breezes, monsoons, and the ITCZ are each illustratable facts, but 'explain' spans three phenomena and the ITCZ is abstract.

G8-L-1.why: The labeled digestive tract with what happens at each stage is the classic illustrated fact (G6-L-1 precedent).

G8-L-2.why: Models, flow charts, and simulations are a heavy representational wrapper; 'digestion absorbs, blood carries, kidneys filter' is card-able but integrative.

G8-L-3.why: Roots absorb, stem carries, leaves use water is a one-illustration plant-transport fact.

G8-L-4.why: Drawing a pedigree is process, but dominant/recessive traits through a family (dimples, earlobes) is a stateable fact.

G8-L-5.why: A Punnett square giving 3:1 is showable, but 'predict ratios' is a calculation best served by a quiz.

G8-L-6.why: Six kingdoms and three domains are a chart fact, but 'importance of' the systems is meta and spans two schemes.

G8-L-7.why: Hair and milk make us mammals, opposable thumbs and forward eyes make us primates is a plain fact.

G8-L-8.why: Flow charts are presentation (G6-M-1 precedent); each cycle is a classic illustration, but three cycles to 'explain' spans several cards.

G8-L-9.why: Photosynthesis and respiration inputs and outputs are a textbook one-illustration fact.

G8-L-10.why: The card is the secondary source; chloroplast for photosynthesis, mitochondria for respiration is a one-sentence fact.

G8-L-11.why: Planning an investigation is a skill (G5-M-9 precedent); the classic foil-and-iodine starch test is a card-able method, the anchor fact is already G8-L-9.

G8-M-1.why: Timeline-making is process, but Dalton-Thomson-Rutherford-Bohr is one side-by-side illustrated fact sequence (G4-L-5 precedent).

G8-M-2.why: Drawing is process, but nucleus plus electron shells is THE classic single illustration (G4-L-7 precedent).

G8-M-3.why: Proton, neutron, electron by symbol, mass, charge, location is a crisp table fact.

G8-M-4.why: Pure substances have fixed composition and each element a unique proton number is a plain fact.

G8-M-5.why: Mendeleev leaving gaps for undiscovered elements is a great fact, but 'contributions of early scientists' spans several people.

G8-M-6.why: Names and symbols of the first 20 elements is pure recall best drilled as a quiz.

G8-M-7.why: 7 periods and 18 groups arranged by atomic structure is factual but abstract for one illustration.

G8-M-8.why: Electron structure determines table position is a one-sentence fact but abstract without shell diagrams.

G8-M-9.why: Atomic number = protons, mass number minus protons = neutrons is a fact, but 'calculate' for several elements is a drill.

G8-M-10.why: Same group, same valence electrons is a one-sentence fact but needs shell diagrams to land.

G8-E-1.why: About 71% of Earth's surface is water is a perfect one-sentence fact.

G8-E-2.why: The card is the secondary source; crust layers (soil, bedrock, continental vs oceanic) are facts, though the target 'upper crustal layers' is loosely specified.

G8-E-3.why: Active/dormant/extinct and shield/cinder/composite volcano types are crisp illustrated facts.

G8-E-4.why: Thick sticky lava builds steep cones, runny lava builds flat ones is a one-illustration fact.

G8-E-5.why: Volcanoes, quakes, and mountain belts line up along plate edges (Ring of Fire) is one classic map illustration.

G8-E-6.why: Oceanic and continental crust ride on lithospheric plates is factual but abstract for one card.

G8-E-7.why: The card is the secondary source; typhoons form over warm seas and the Philippines sits in their path is a classic fact.

G8-E-8.why: Plotting tracking data on a map is a skill; a card can only show what the PAR boundary is and a sample track.

G8-E-9.why: Warm seas feed typhoons and mountains weaken them is a one-illustration fact.

G8-E-10.why: The card is the secondary source; PAGASA warnings, evacuation centers, and relief are stateable, though civic rather than science content.

G8-E-11.why: Moon and Sun pull causing high and low tides is a classic one-illustration fact.

G8-E-12.why: The card is the secondary source; tidal barrages and the San Bernardino Strait potential are facts, though 'identify situations' is open-ended.

G8-F-1.why: Force causes acceleration, acceleration is rate of change of velocity, is a one-sentence fact.

G8-F-2.why: Observing locally is a wrapper (G4-F-10 precedent); a jeepney pulling away or a tricycle rounding a corner are generic illustrated facts.

G8-F-3.why: Constructing and annotating motion graphs is a skill (G4-F-4 precedent); a card can only show what a curved line means.

G8-F-4.why: Kinetic is moving, potential is stored by position is a classic one-illustration fact.

G8-F-5.why: Swing and roller-coaster KE/PE swaps are per-example illustrated facts.

G8-F-6.why: Work is done only when a force moves something is a one-sentence fact.

G8-F-7.why: Power is how fast work is done is a one-sentence fact.

G8-F-8.why: Mechanical energy = KE + PE is a one-sentence fact but an abstract sum with no natural illustration.

G8-F-9.why: A falling mango trades height for speed with total energy kept is a strong illustrated fact.

G8-F-10.why: The card is the secondary source; Angat or Magat dam water turning turbines is a great Philippine illustrated fact.

G8-F-11.why: Guided investigation is process, but mirror reflection and lens/prism refraction are strong facts (G6-F-5 precedent).

G9-F-1.why: Inertia as the tendency to keep doing what it is doing is a one-sentence fact.

G9-F-2.why: 'Demonstrate in practical situations' is process, but net force changes speed or direction is a stateable fact (G4-F-5 precedent).

G9-F-3.why: 'Investigate the relationship' is the competency (G5-F-2 precedent); F = ma is only the wrapped result.

G9-F-4.why: Every push gets an equal opposite push is a classic one-illustration fact.

G9-F-5.why: Stepping off a boat as an action-reaction pair is a fact, but drawing force diagrams to explain it is a skill.

G9-F-6.why: Electricity is flowing electrons plus safety tips are plain stateable facts.

G9-F-7.why: Guided circuit investigations to infer V, I, R relationships is hands-on (G5-F-8 precedent); Ohm's law is only the wrapped result.

G9-F-8.why: Assembling circuits with meters is a skill; a card can show circuit symbols and one sample diagram (G5-F-8 precedent).

G9-F-9.why: Class discussion is the medium, not the source (G6-E-3 precedent); series lights all die together while parallel house wiring does not is a crisp fact.

G9-F-10.why: EMR from vibrating charges travelling as transverse waves is a one-sentence fact but abstract for one illustration.

G9-F-11.why: The EM spectrum from radio to gamma by wavelength is one classic illustration.

G9-F-12.why: Radio for phones, x-rays for bones are per-example illustrated facts.

G9-F-13.why: The card is the secondary source; UV sunburn and x-ray dose limits are plain facts.

G9-E-1.why: Matching coastlines, fossils, and rocks as Pangaea evidence is a classic illustrated fact.

G9-E-2.why: Collaborative group task is process and the area is national not personal; the Philippine and Manila Trenches as boundary evidence are facts.

G9-E-3.why: Convergent, divergent, transform boundaries is the classic three-panel illustration.

G9-E-4.why: Index fossils date rock layers is a one-illustration fact.

G9-E-5.why: Relative (layer order) vs absolute (radioactive decay) dating is factual but abstract and spans two methods.

G9-E-6.why: The geologic time scale as Earth's calendar is a timeline illustration, but 'explain how it helps recount history' is meta.

G9-E-7.why: S-waves not passing the liquid outer core is a good did-you-know, but the inference chain is abstract for one card.

G9-E-8.why: Scale drawing is a skill, but layer thicknesses (crust ~5-70 km, mantle ~2,900 km) with a cutaway illustration is a fact.

G9-E-9.why: Comet vs meteoroid vs asteroid vs dwarf planet are crisp facts, but 'how they help understand Solar System formation' is abstract.

G9-E-10.why: The card is the secondary source; meteor showers recur when Earth crosses comet debris (Perseids, Geminids) is a plain fact.

G9-E-11.why: Hubble, JWST, and Voyager probes studying space is a per-example illustrated fact.

G9-L-1.why: Model-making is process, but the double helix is THE classic single illustration (G4-L-7 precedent).

G9-L-2.why: Chromosomes hold DNA, DNA holds genes, genes carry traits is a nested one-illustration fact.

G9-L-3.why: Mutations as DNA changes caused by radiation, chemicals, or infections is a plain fact.

G9-L-4.why: The card is the secondary source; sickle-cell protecting against malaria is a great beneficial/harmful fact.

G9-L-5.why: A mixed forest surviving a pest that kills one tree kind is card-able, but 'explain the advantage during difficult conditions' spans several cases.

G9-L-6.why: The card is the secondary source; tamaraw critically endangered, Philippine eagle critically endangered is classification best drilled as classify-this.

G9-L-7.why: Class discussion is the medium, but habitat loss and hunting leading to extinction is broad content for one card.

G9-L-8.why: Secondary sources make it the G6-E-2 pattern, not local-inquiry; generic conservation actions (no hunting, plant mangroves) are facts, the learner's own local species are not.

G9-L-9.why: Labeled diagrams are presentation; biotic and abiotic features of each named ecosystem is a crisp per-ecosystem illustrated fact.

G9-L-10.why: The card is the secondary source; janitor fish in Laguna de Bay or deforestation effects are plain facts.

G9-L-11.why: Planning a survey is pure process (G4-M-7 precedent).

G9-M-1.why: Carrying out a valid investigation is the competency; limewater turning milky with CO2 is only the wrapped method fact.

G9-M-2.why: Bonds breaking and forming makes a new substance is a one-sentence fact but abstract for one illustration.

G9-M-3.why: Valence electron as outer-shell bonding electron is a one-sentence fact but needs a shell diagram to land.

G9-M-4.why: Oxygen in Group 16 has 6 valence electrons is a lookup fact best checked as a quick quiz.

G9-M-5.why: Sodium giving one electron to chlorine to make table salt is a classic single illustration.

G9-M-6.why: NaCl, MgO, KCl, MgCl2 names and formulas are recall, but 'write the formula' edges into a derivation skill.

G9-M-7.why: Shared electrons in water and carbon dioxide is a classic one-illustration fact.

G9-M-8.why: H2O, CO2, NH3 names and formulas are pure recall best drilled as a quiz.

G9-M-9.why: 'Show using models' is process, but salt crystal lattice vs individual water molecules is one illustrated fact.

G9-M-10.why: Sea-of-electrons explaining conductivity and malleability is one illustration but abstract.

G9-M-11.why: 'Investigate the properties of ionic, covalent, and metallic substances, such as melting point, hardness, electrical and thermal conductivity' — the properties are enumerated in the text and are the assessable knowledge (ionic: high melting point, conducts only when molten/dissolved; covalent: low melting point, non-conductor; metallic: conducts, malleable). This matches G6-F-5 ('carry out investigations ... observe and describe the features including crests, troughs ...' = mixed 3) more than G6-F-3 ('carry out fair tests to show how levers ...' = process 2), which the original cited. A one-illustration three-column property table is a natural card; the investigation wrapper caps it at 3.

G10-E-1.why: GPS and satellites measuring plates moving a few cm per year is a great did-you-know fact.

G10-E-2.why: What happens at each boundary type (trench, ridge, fault) is a per-type illustrated fact.

G10-E-3.why: A Philippine map of mountains, faults, volcanoes, and trenches is the card itself, but one illustration is dense and 'interpret' spans features.

G10-E-4.why: 'Predict' is a calculation, but 'the Philippine Plate moves ~8 cm/yr so in 50 My it shifts ~4,000 km' is a card-able fact.

G10-E-5.why: The card is the secondary source; mantle convection, slab pull, and the soft asthenosphere are facts but abstract for one illustration.

G10-E-6.why: Subduction making volcanoes, trenches, and quakes on the upper plate is a classic one-illustration fact.

G10-E-7.why: Colliding plates pushed up the Himalayas and Andes is a plain illustrated fact.

G10-E-8.why: Rising temperatures, melting ice, rising seas as evidence are plain facts.

G10-E-9.why: Greenhouse gases trapping heat is the classic one-illustration fact.

G10-E-10.why: El Nino bringing drought to the Philippines is a strong stateable fact.

G10-E-11.why: Identifying the learner's own local impacts is inquiry, but Philippine-generic impacts and individual actions are facts (G4-M-6 precedent).

G10-E-12.why: Philippine geothermal, solar, and wind (Bangui) cutting emissions is a plain illustrated fact.

G10-F-1.why: Investigating with basketballs is process, but 45 degrees gives the longest throw is a stateable fact.

G10-F-2.why: Bouncing balls (elastic) vs crumpling cars (inelastic) is a per-example illustrated fact.

G10-F-3.why: Using models to investigate is process, but the forces and effects in collisions are describable facts.

G10-F-4.why: Momentum grows with mass and speed, so a truck hits harder than a bike, is a one-illustration fact.

G10-F-5.why: Carrying out guided investigations is the competency; 'more momentum, harder to stop' is already covered by G10-F-4 (G5-E-7 precedent).

G10-F-6.why: Catching a ball with bent arms spreads force over time is a good card, but force-over-time (impulse) is a two-variable abstraction.

G10-F-7.why: The card is the secondary source; seatbelts, airbags, crumple zones are per-example illustrated facts.

G10-F-8.why: Total momentum before equals after (billiard balls) is a one-sentence fact but abstract for one illustration.

G10-F-9.why: Power plant to transmission lines to substation to meter is one classic chain illustration.

G10-F-10.why: Household electrical safety precautions are plain stateable tips.

G10-F-11.why: A motor turns electricity into motion, a generator the reverse with the same parts, is one crisp illustrated fact.

G10-F-12.why: Class discussion is the medium; LED bulbs, inverter aircon, and unplugging chargers with their benefits are crisp Filipino-household facts.

G10-F-13.why: The card is the secondary source; coal vs geothermal impacts in the Philippines are facts, but 'evaluate' is broad.

G10-M-1.why: Color change, gas, precipitate, odor, temperature as reaction signs is a crisp illustrated fact.

G10-M-2.why: Indicator testing is hands-on, but HCl acid, NaOH base, saline salt, and indicator colors are facts best drilled as classify-this.

G10-M-3.why: Combination, decomposition, single and double replacement are facts, but four abstract patterns need one card each.

G10-M-4.why: The card is the secondary source; rusting, acid rain on marble, combustion smoke are facts, but 'explain how they impact environments' spans many.

G10-M-5.why: 'Scientists use equations' is a fact, but writing word and formula equations is method knowledge a card can only illustrate with one example.

G10-M-6.why: Atoms are only rearranged so total mass stays the same is a one-illustration fact.

G10-M-7.why: Balancing chemical equations is a pen-and-paper calculation, not a science-process skill in the scheme's sense (investigating, measuring, graphing, equipment, debating, collaborating). The original itself classified the sibling calculation competencies G7-M-9 (express concentration quantitatively) and G8-M-9 (calculate protons/neutrons/electrons) as mixed 3 quiz; G10-M-7 is the same class and should match. A card can show '2H2 + O2 -> 2H2O: 4 H and 2 O on each side' as one illustration, and a balance-this quiz drills it; keep card_form quiz.

G10-M-8.why: Refrigeration slows spoilage, fanning feeds fire are crisp facts, but four factors across five applications spans many cards.

G10-M-9.why: Exothermic gives off heat, endothermic absorbs it (burning vs instant cold pack) is a one-illustration fact.

G10-L-1.why: Homeostasis as body balance with temperature, glucose, blood pressure as indicators is a plain fact.

G10-L-2.why: Sweating to cool down as negative feedback is illustratable, but positive vs negative feedback is abstract for one card.

G10-L-3.why: The card is the secondary source; better-suited individuals survive and breed (peppered moth) is a classic illustrated fact.

G10-L-4.why: Small-group discussion is the medium, but variation, heredity, isolation, selection, adaptation are five abstract concepts for cards.

G10-L-5.why: The card is the secondary source; homologous forelimbs and fossils are illustratable, but 'explain how lines of evidence support' is reasoning-heavy.

G10-L-6.why: Biotechnology as using living things to make products, with examples, is a one-sentence fact.

G10-L-7.why: The card is the secondary source; nata de coco and vinegar made by microbes is a great Filipino illustrated fact.

G10-L-8.why: The card is the secondary source; Bt corn, Golden Rice, IVF are per-example illustrated facts.

G10-L-9.why: Participating in a debate is pure process; GMO pros and cons are only the wrapped content half.

G10-L-10.why: 'Discuss' is a classroom verb; food, water, shelter, mates limiting a population is a plain illustrated fact.

G10-L-11.why: Growth slowing near carrying capacity is a one-sentence fact but an S-curve concept that leans on a graph.
